title: C482/425/2012 of DR. DEEPAK KALRA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application (C482) No. 425 of 2012
Dr. Deepak Kalra, S/o Late Sri R.R. Kalra, R/o 2-B,
Preetam Road, Dalanwala, Dehradun.

Versus
1. State of Uttarakhand, through Secretory Home,
Dehradun.
2. Special Judicial Magistrate (C.B.I.), Dehradun.
3. Guru Charan Suri, S/o T.R. Suri.
R/o 2-B, Preetam Road, Dehradun.

......Respondents
Mr. S.S. Yadav, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, Brief Holder, present for the State.
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.

Heard.
2) By means of this petition moved under
Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the petitioner has sought
quashing of the proceedings of Criminal Complaint Case
No. 5832 of 2010, Guru Charan Suri Vs. Dr. Deepak
Kalra, relating to offence punishable under Section 138
of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, pending in the
court of Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Dehradun.

2
3) Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted
that the complainant (respondent No.3) Guru Charan
Suri dishonestly represented himself as the sole owner of
the property, while executing the agreement of sale with
the petitioner. In fact, he is said to be only one of the co-owners.
4) However, from the perusal of the contents of
the petition and other papers on record, it is clear that
agreement of sale was executed between the petitioner
and the respondent No.3, and it is also admitted that the
petitioner had issued cheques to the respondent No.3 and
impugned cheque no 395618 dated 04.10.2009, for an
amount of Rs. 14,400/- was dishonoured on presentation
before the bankers, on the ground of "stop payment"
direction. The summoning order is being challenged after
a period of one and half years.
5) In the circumstances, this Court is not
inclined to interfere with the trial of the case. As to the
factual pleas of defence, the petitioner is at liberty to take
the same before the trial court.
6) Accordingly, the petition under Section 482
of Cr.P.C., is dismissed, with the observation that the

3
trial court shall consider the factual pleas of defence of
the petitioner, and shall decide the case as expeditiously
as possible, keeping in mind the spirit contained in sub-Section (3) of Section 143 of the Act.
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
03.05.2012
JM
